punchline: Legend says a poet named the crushed guests of a banquet by remembering where each one had sat.
thirty_sec: The Greek poet Simonides was called out of a banquet just before the roof fell in. The guests could not be recognised, but he remembered where each had sat, and the dead were identified. That legend is credited as the start of the memory palace, which Joshua Foer used in the year of training that led to his 2006 USA title.
